note: Fifty texts from Hispanic_Reunification_Canon_data.json, each joined to its author record. Built by tools/build-canon-works.py; author names are the ones each is known by.

name.es: La independencia y las primeras uniones

works.title: Carta de Jamaica
works.author: Simón Bolívar
works.fullName: Simón José Antonio de la Santísima Trinidad Bolívar Palacios
works.region: Venezuela; Colombia; wider northern South America
works.position: Bolívar imagined American cooperation amid war and fragmentation but doubted simple continental political unity. Strong executive power, slavery and racial order complicate later egalitarian appropriations.

works.title: Soñaba el abad de San Pedro, y yo también sé soñar
works.author: José Cecilio del Valle
works.position: Valle proposed a practical American congress and cooperation in knowledge and prosperity. His Central American location disrupts a genealogy beginning and ending with Bolívar.

works.title: Gramática de la lengua castellana destinada al uso de los americanos: prologue and related cultural writings
works.author: Andrés Bello
works.fullName: Andrés de Jesús María y José Bello López
works.position: Bello defended a shared language while asserting the legitimacy of American usage and institutions. Linguistic continuity after independence does not mean a wish to restore Spanish sovereignty.

works.title: El Estado federal de Panamá
works.author: Justo Arosemena
works.position: Arosemena justified local political autonomy within wider constitutional association. The canal corridor makes sovereignty and scale concrete, complicating abstract calls for unity.

works.title: Iniciativa de la América: idea de un Congreso Federal de las Repúblicas
works.author: Francisco Bilbao
works.position: Bilbao's continental language emerged amid U.S. expansion and filibustering, yet also opposed European domination. His anti-clerical republicanism conflicts with Catholic Hispanidad.

works.title: Unión latino-americana, pensamiento de Bolívar para formar una liga americana
works.author: José María Torres Caicedo
works.position: Torres Caicedo helped popularize Latin America through poetry, diplomacy and organized association. His project differs from both Bilbao's radical republicanism and French imperial Pan-Latinism.

works.title: Os brahamanes
works.author: Francisco Luís Gomes
works.camp: Liberal Catholic anti-caste and antislavery argument
works.position: A Goan parliamentarian and novelist who criticized caste and British power through Portuguese literary forms. His Catholic universalism can coexist with colonial assumptions requiring scrutiny.

works.title: Ojeada histórico-crítica sobre la poesía ecuatoriana, desde su época más remota hasta nuestros días
works.author: Juan León Mera
works.position: Mera sought Ecuadorian literary identity through Spanish-language continuity and mediated Indigenous materials. Catholic nationality and American distinctiveness coexist uneasily.

works.title: Antillean federation essays and speeches: new selection
works.author: Eugenio María de Hostos
works.fullName: Eugenio María de Hostos y Bonilla
works.position: Hostos joined Antillean freedom, education and moral sociology. Federation served island sovereignty against empires, including Spain, rather than restoration of colonial unity.

works.title: História da civilização ibérica
works.author: Oliveira Martins
works.position: His civilizational narrative treated Spain and Portugal within an Iberian historical field while retaining national differentiation. Economic and racial explanations should be read critically.

works.title: O abolicionismo
works.author: Joaquim Nabuco
works.fullName: Joaquim Aurélio Barreto Nabuco de Araújo
works.camp: Abolitionist liberalism; monarchy and later Pan-American diplomacy
works.position: Nabuco's abolitionism attacks the social foundation hidden beneath idealized Luso-Brazilian continuity. His later U.S.-oriented diplomacy complicates an automatically anti-Anglo Brazilian canon.

works.title: Filipinas dentro de cien años
works.author: José Rizal
works.fullName: José Protasio Rizal Mercado y Alonso Realonda
works.camp: Reformist anticolonial critique; Spanish-language Filipino authorship
works.position: Rizal used Spanish to criticize colonial domination and imagine Philippine futures. Language affiliation does not make him a supporter of Spanish imperial restoration; his positions developed under changing conditions.

works.title: Nuestra América
works.author: José Martí
works.position: Martí grounded American self-government in knowledge of local peoples and histories, opposed colonial domination and criticized racial antagonism. His love of Spanish language did not imply political subordination to Spain.

works.title: Pájinas libres
works.author: Manuel González Prada
works.camp: Radical liberalism to anarchism; Indigenous-critical precursor
works.position: He attacked oligarchy, clericalism and the exclusion of Indigenous peoples. His critique was a resource for later radical national thought without making him identical to Mariátegui.

works.title: En torno al casticismo
works.author: Miguel de Unamuno
works.camp: Liberal, existential and religious Hispanism; politically changeable
works.position: A Basque-born Salamanca intellectual located cultural continuity in lived language, intrahistory and spiritual struggle. His European and American correspondence makes him a transatlantic interlocutor, not a consistent programmatic Catholic nationalist.

works.title: Idearium español
works.author: Ángel Ganivet
works.position: A diplomat and essayist who interpreted Spain's crisis through historical psychology, geographical conditions and spiritual energy. Withdrawal from failed external domination could support cultural renewal.

works.title: El triunfo de Calibán and hemispheric writings
works.author: Rubén Darío
works.camp: Modernismo; changing Latin and Hispanic solidarities
works.position: Darío's poetry and journalism express competing attitudes toward Spain, Latin America and the United States. The shift between Roosevelt and the eagle poem is essential evidence against a fixed anti-U.S. creed.

works.title: Ariel
works.author: José Enrique Rodó
works.position: Rodó urged educated youth to reconcile democratic society with cultivated spiritual and aesthetic life. His critique of utilitarianism is not a complete anti-imperialist political program; his selective elitism also matters.

works.title: Carácter de la literatura del Perú independiente
works.author: José de la Riva-Agüero
works.fullName: José de la Riva-Agüero y Osma
works.camp: From liberal aristocratic criticism to Catholic authoritarian Hispanism
works.position: His early literary history privileged Hispanic continuity; later political and religious commitments became markedly more reactionary. The chronology matters: the 1905 thesis is not a transparent statement of his final politics.

works.title: A América Latina: males de origem
works.author: Manoel do Bomfim
works.position: Bomfim shifted explanation from racial inferiority to historical exploitation and social parasitism. His inclusion makes Brazil an active critic of imperial racial narratives, not simply a supplier of Lusotropicalism.

works.title: Creación de la pedagogía nacional
works.author: Franz Tamayo
works.camp: National pedagogy; racialized valorization of Indigenous vitality
works.position: Tamayo rejected imported pedagogy and valorized Indigenous strength, while retaining racial typologies and elite mediation. He is not straightforwardly an Indigenous liberation theorist.

works.title: La creación de un continente
works.author: Francisco García Calderón
works.position: He argued for Latin American civilizational consolidation while drawing on elite liberalism and racial hierarchies. His original French book reveals the role of Paris in American self-definition.

works.title: La leyenda negra y la verdad histórica
works.author: Julián Juderías
works.position: Juderías analyzed adverse images of Spain and made the Black Legend a durable historiographic category. His account must itself be tested against archives and earlier uses of the phrase.

works.title: España y el programa americanista
works.author: Rafael Altamira
works.position: A historian, jurist and international educator who pursued Spanish-American rapprochement through universities, pedagogy and law. Cultural cooperation could replace political empire, although the asymmetry of Spain's civilizing claim remained an issue.

works.title: La caída del águila
works.author: Carlos Gagini
works.position: A linguist and novelist imagined resistance to U.S. domination through speculative geopolitical fiction. Central American agency and the role of non-Iberian powers prevent easy classification as Spain-centered Hispanidad.

works.title: El destino de un continente
works.author: Manuel Ugarte
works.position: Ugarte described fragmented American republics as vulnerable to external domination and sought solidarity across Spanish America. His evolving relation to socialism and nationalism requires chronological treatment.

works.title: A aliança peninsular: antecedentes e possibilidades
works.author: António Sardinha
works.position: Sardinha proposed a spiritual and geopolitical alliance of distinct Iberian nations. He resisted liberal federal amalgamation: Portuguese sovereignty and Catholic-monarchical tradition were constitutive, not temporary obstacles.

works.title: La unidad de la América Indo-Española and related essays
works.author: José Carlos Mariátegui
works.position: Mariátegui accepted a shared historical matrix while insisting that land, class and Indigenous life determine the prospects of emancipation. His Indo-Spanish vocabulary is neither proof of Maeztu-style Hispanidad nor an erasure of conquest.

works.title: Eurindia: ensayo de estética fundado en la experiencia histórica de las culturas americanas
works.author: Ricardo Rojas
works.position: Rojas proposed an aesthetic synthesis of European and Indigenous inheritances. His inclusive language coexists with the authority of a national elite deciding the terms of synthesis.

works.title: La raza cósmica: misión de la raza iberoamericana. Notas de viajes a la América del Sur
works.author: José Vasconcelos
works.camp: Revolutionary cultural mission; later conservative Catholic and authoritarian turns
works.position: His future Ibero-American race combines anti-Anglo imperial rivalry, education and spiritual aesthetics with eugenic and hierarchical assumptions. Later political positions cannot be smuggled into every earlier sentence, or omitted from reception.

works.title: Seis ensayos en busca de nuestra expresión
works.author: Pedro Henríquez Ureña
works.region: Dominican Republic; Mexico; United States; Argentina
works.position: A Dominican scholar sought American literary expression within a broad humanist culture. His migration and work in several languages undermine a simple center-periphery literary model.

works.title: Plan de realización del supremo sueño de Bolívar
works.author: Augusto César Sandino
works.position: Sandino linked resistance to U.S. occupation with concrete continental security and cooperation proposals. Its political and spiritual context should not be reduced to later party canonization.

works.title: El mínimum vital
works.author: Alberto Masferrer
works.camp: Vitalismo; social reform and unionist milieu
works.position: Masferrer's social ethics make basic subsistence, labor and education the test of civilization. His relevance is social and regional, not an automatic claim that every work advances Hispanic federation.

works.title: Insularismo: ensayos de interpretación puertorriqueña
works.author: Antonio S. Pedreira
works.position: Pedreira diagnosed Puerto Rico's cultural condition under U.S. sovereignty through geography, history and Hispanic inheritance. His account's racial and gender hierarchies are central problems, not peripheral blemishes.

works.title: Defensa de la Hispanidad
works.author: Ramiro de Maeztu
works.position: A journalist whose trajectory ran from regenerationism and guild-socialist interests to counterrevolutionary Catholicism. The mature argument makes a universal religious mission, rather than biological purity, the basis of Hispanic solidarity, while defending hierarchy and Spanish imperial memory.

works.title: El antiimperialismo y el APRA
works.author: Víctor Raúl Haya de la Torre
works.fullName: Víctor Raúl Haya de la Torre
works.position: Haya proposed continental anti-imperialist organization and a broad social coalition adapted to Indo-American conditions. The economic role of imperialism and the stages of revolution separated him from communist critics.

works.title: Pensamiento y poesía en la vida española
works.author: María Zambrano
works.position: Her exile philosophy reimagined Spanish cultural experience through poetic reason, spiritual inquiry and criticism of European catastrophe. Religious language did not make her a Francoist Hispanist.

works.title: Contrapunteo cubano del tabaco y el azúcar
works.author: Fernando Ortiz
works.camp: Transculturation; Afro-Cuban studies; changing racial thought
works.position: Ortiz moved from racialized criminology toward a dynamic account of cultural formation. Transculturation describes conflict and transformation more precisely than an uncomplicated fusion narrative.

works.title: O mundo que o português criou
works.author: Gilberto Freyre
works.region: Brazil; Portugal; colonial Africa and Asia
works.position: Freyre interpreted Brazilian formation through household, slavery, sexuality and mixture, then elaborated a transcontinental Portuguese tropical vocation. Recognition of African cultural contributions coexists with paternalism and minimization of coercion.

works.title: Hispanoamérica del dolor
works.author: Jaime Eyzaguirre
works.position: Eyzaguirre interpreted Hispanic America through a religious and historical vocation marked by suffering. His compact prose gives Catholic Hispanism an American, not merely Spanish, center.

works.title: América como conciencia
works.author: Leopoldo Zea
works.position: Zea defended Latin American philosophical self-understanding through historical experience. His universalism seeks participation from a situated perspective rather than abstract imitation.

works.title: Qu'est-ce que le luso-tropicalisme?
works.author: Mário Pinto de Andrade
works.camp: Anticolonial cultural criticism; African Lusophone networks
works.position: Andrade criticized the ideological concealment of colonial domination and helped constitute African Portuguese-language literary networks. His French-language interventions make the genealogy explicitly multilingual.

works.title: Cabo Verde visto por Gilberto Freyre: apontamentos lidos ao microfone de Rádio Barlavento
works.author: Baltasar Lopes
works.camp: Creole cultural identity; criticism of Freyre
works.position: Lopes challenged Freyre's reading of Cape Verde and asserted a more specific island social and linguistic formation. His criticism does not automatically equal Cabral's revolutionary program.

works.title: Um Fernando Pessoa
works.author: Agostinho da Silva
works.position: Exile in Brazil and educational experiments sustained a non-reductive spiritual vision of Portuguese cultural destiny. His universalism cannot simply be absorbed into Salazar's imperial program.

works.title: El Uruguay como problema: en la cuenca del Plata entre Argentina y Brasil
works.author: Alberto Methol Ferré
works.camp: Catholic, national-popular and regional integration thought
works.position: Methol made Uruguay's position between Argentina and Brazil a problem of regional scale, sovereignty and industrial development. His Catholicism coexists with national-popular continental politics.

works.title: Historia de la nación latinoamericana
works.author: Jorge Abelardo Ramos
works.position: Ramos redescribed separate republics as fragments of a larger historical nation and interpreted imperial dependency through left-nationalist politics. His rehabilitation of aspects of Hispanic inheritance differs from Catholic Hispanidad.

works.title: National Liberation and Culture / Libertação nacional e cultura
works.author: Amílcar Cabral
works.camp: Anticolonial revolutionary humanism; culture and liberation
works.position: Cabral treated culture as a field of colonial domination and collective resistance. Portuguese could be used instrumentally without accepting Portuguese imperial tutelage.

works.title: Historia y tragedia de Guinea Ecuatorial
works.author: Donato Ndongo
works.position: Ndongo uses Spanish to analyze both colonial domination and post-independence dictatorship. His Hispanic literary affiliation is compatible with fierce criticism of Spain and local authoritarianism.

works.title: Culture and History: Occasional Notes on the Process of Philippine Becoming
works.author: Nick Joaquín
works.position: Joaquín interpreted Philippine formation through transformations produced by Hispanic contact. Writing in English and recognizing historical creation makes him different from a campaign simply to restore Spanish-language dominance.

works.title: A nau de Ícaro, seguido de Imagem e miragem da lusofonia
works.author: Eduardo Lourenço
works.position: Lourenço examined Portuguese self-mythology and the temptation to imagine Lusophony as an empire surviving in language. Cultural affinity must confront asymmetry and divergent histories.
